svg.title: Iterated Seesaw Double-Chain Rectangle in Stage 03 (SeesawIdentity.lean)
svg.desc: Editorial mathematical diagram of the two-track seesaw rectangle proved in New.Data.seesaw_identity (src/New/UpperBound/Seesaw/SeesawIdentity.lean). Both paths begin at the definite base unitary space X_0 (rank k = r + 1 - m) carrying a ramified source form phi in ramifiedSourceForms and meet at the common definite destination Y_m (rank n_m - 1 = r + mt, Y_m subset of X_m). The upper definite track (cobalt, solid borders) lifts phi across m = 2*varrho + 2 definite spaces X_0 to X_1 (rank k + t + 1) through varrho + 1 glued double lifts to X_m (rank n_m = r + mt + 1) with a glued chain datum Psi satisfying IsChainDatum theta Psi (admissible support, integral away from theta.normQ, l1-bounded when theta.Q = empty, jointly levelX j-invariant), then restricts via D.restrictToY (restrictToFormY) down to Y_m to produce compositeLift theta Psi phi. The lower indefinite-to-definite track (emerald, dashed borders on indefinite spaces) descends from X_0 to Y_0 (rank r, indefinite signature with varrho hyperbolic planes plus <-N>) via the Poincare map P = poincareAt g t (Riesz representative of the Bessel period on R_0), then lifts via adelic theta lifts liftY theta j through Y_1 (rank r + t) and signature shifts to definite Y_m, producing lowerChain theta (P phi). Inside the rectangle sits the amber Seesaw Unfolding Engine pairing the lower track against an arbitrary test form z in ConjFormY in three steps: (1) Transposed descent via transposedLiftY theta j (exact adjoint integral_mul_liftY) walks z down from Y_m to Y_0; (2) Iterated Bessel unfolding of unfoldedPeriod Xi_{k+1} via integral_unfoldStageOn_mul_transposedLiftY and induction (exists_integral_mul_lowerChainUpTo_eq_cutSum) reduces each outer integral to a finite coset sum cutSum over Omega_0 x ... x Omega_k with denominators confined to theta.normQ; (3) Tensor assembly forms seesawDatum theta (isInvariant_seesawDatum, exists_isAdmissibleCombination_seesawDatum), supplying the upper chain datum Psi. The closing banner states New.Data.seesaw_identity: lowerChain theta (P phi) = c * compositeLift theta Psi phi for one single twist-independent nonzero scalar c in C^x across all twists theta and ramified source forms phi, alongside a rust honesty callout noting the non-vanishing boundary: c != 0 is proved here via normUnit, whereas non-vanishing and spanning of the Poincare image belong to Theorem B (Stage 04).

g.text: Iterated Seesaw Double-Chain Rectangle in SeesawIdentity.lean
◆ UPPER TRACK · DEFINITE CHAIN (m = 2ϱ + 2 lifts glued into ϱ + 1 double lifts)
IsChainDatum ϑ Ψ : admissible support · integral away from ϑ.normQ · ℓ1-bounded if ϑ.Q = ∅ · jointly levelX j-invariant
supplies glued datum Ψ (IsChainDatum ϑ Ψ)
pair z ∈ ConjFormY with lowerChain ϑ (P φ)
Walks test form z ∈ ConjFormY down from Ym to Y0 to meet P φ
Finite coset sum cutSum over Ω0 × ⋯ × Ωk · denoms ∣ ϑ.normQ
● LOWER TRACK · INDEFINITE-TO-DEFINITE CHAIN (adelic lifts liftY ϑ j)
∀ ϑ : Twist, ∃ Ψ (IsChainDatum ϑ Ψ), ∀ φ ∈ ramifiedSourceForms
lowerChain ϑ (P φ) = c • compositeLift ϑ Ψ φ
Same c for all twists ϑ & ramified φ (only Ψ varies with ϑ)
c ∈ ℂ× is global; Ψ depends on ϑ (denoms ∣ ϑ.normQ)
ℓ1-bound on Ψ holds at trivial twist (ϑ.Q = ∅)
c ≠ 0 is proved here (normUnit); neither side is proved nonzero.
Non-vanishing & spanning of the image belong to Theorem B (Stage 04).
